h: Tulip vases, a famous film and a walk on the Cotswold Way
p: William Blathwayt was a busy man at the court of William III, serving as Secretary at War, and his travels and Dutch connections shaped the taste of the whole house. Keep an eye out for the Delftware, including towering tulip vases, which show just how fashionable Dutch style was at the time. They are a lovely talking point, especially if you have anyone in the group who loves pottery or flowers.

Film fans might feel a flicker of recognition, too. Dyrham was one of the locations for The Remains of the Day, the 1993 film with Anthony Hopkins and Emma Thompson, and the long views down the park have a properly cinematic feel.

Next to the house is the little parish church of St Peter, which makes a peaceful detour if you like old village churches. The long-distance Cotswold Way also passes close to the estate, so keen walkers can stretch their legs on a bit of the trail before or after their visit.

How long to allow? Half a day works well for the house, gardens and a stroll in the park, but on a sunny day you could easily stay longer with a picnic. Bring sturdy footwear if you plan to tackle the slopes.

Combine it with Bath for a classic double: the Roman Baths, the sweep of the Royal Crescent and the shops around Milsom Street are all a short drive away. Alternatively, head west towards Bristol for a buzzing evening by the harbourside.
